theater: 巴爾幹山關與色雷斯邊境

battle.name: 莫里斯的巴爾幹戰役
battle.theater: 巴爾幹山關與色雷斯邊境
battle.brief: 公元582年秋末，東羅馬帝國的莫里斯率色雷斯與安納托利亞的野戰軍南下，進入巴爾幹山關的通道，迫使圍困塞薩洛尼基的阿瓦爾聯軍解除包圍、撤回多瑙河北。卡面這名希臘重步兵所代表的方陣盾牆已非實存兵種，但重裝步兵結陣、盾相接、矛齊舉的傳統，正是六世紀帝國步兵仍在沿用的核心。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 582年的這場戰役，形式上是東羅馬帝國的野戰軍與阿瓦爾可汗國聯軍在色雷斯北境的一場對峙，實質上是拜占庭與草原霸權在多瑙河上游的一次正面碰撞。羅馬一方由莫里斯以內廷警長兼「不記名冊的 Comes」的身分領軍，兵源橫跨數個軍區：駐塞薩洛尼基與色雷斯平原的色雷斯主題、安納托利亞主題、直屬君士坦丁堡的歐比克翁、亞美尼亞主題，以及禁衛軍的三個塔格瑪（近衛重步兵、禁衛重騎兵與輕裝禁衛）；另有安納托利亞方面以私人財力供養的私兵 Bucellarii，以及披重甲的卡塔弗拉克托重騎兵、弓兵與操作張力弩的射手。塞薩洛尼基城內有城防軍與民兵守牆，市政議會與守軍共同承擔糧秣調配。阿瓦爾一方是可汗率領的草原聯軍，核心為阿瓦爾騎兵，配屬為數不少的斯拉夫人與格皮德人；拉文納殘卷所載此際的可汗名為巴顏。雙方力量結構極不對稱：羅馬有城垣、有糧道、有成型的兵制，卻缺乏足以在開闊草原上正面壓倒騎兵的衝鋒力量；阿瓦爾有速度、有弓術，卻沒有攻破狄奧多西城牆的攻城技術，也不打算為一座城池長期耗下去。這正是羅馬選擇在山關隘道出手、以地形抵消對手機動優勢的緣由。
countriesEn: The campaign of 582 was in form a confrontation between the field army of the Eastern Roman Empire and a confederated host of the Avar Khaganate on the northern edge of Thrace, and in substance a direct collision between Byzantium and the steppe power on the upper Danube. The Roman side was led by Maurice, who held the office of magister officiorum together with the title of a comes in absentia, and drew its men from several military districts: the Thracian theme stationed at Thessalonica and across the Thracian plain, the Anatolikon theme, the Opsikion with its direct tie to Constantinople, the Armeniakon theme, and the three tagmata of the palace guard (the heavy infantry Scholai, the Excubitores and the light-armed Immuniti); to these were added the Bucellarii, private troops raised and paid for in Anatolia, together with heavily armoured kataphraktoi cavalry, archers and crews of the tension bow. Inside Thessalonica a garrison and the enrolled militia held the walls, and the city council shared with the garrison the task of distributing provisions. The Avar side was a steppe confederation led by the kagan, its core being the Avar cavalry, with a substantial number of Slavs and Gepids attached; the Ravenna Fragment gives the name of the kagan at this time as Bayan. The two structures of force were badly mismatched. Rome had walls, a supply line and a formed military system, but lacked the weight to crush cavalry head-on in open grassland; the Avars had speed and archery, but had no siegecraft capable of breaching the Theodosian walls and no intention of wearing themselves out over a single city. That was precisely why Rome chose to strike in the passes, using the ground to cancel out the enemy's advantage in mobility.
people: 此役留下姓名的核心人物是莫里斯（Flavius Tiberius Mauricius Emperor，約538年生，602年遇害）。他出身色雷斯的拉丁家族，在福卡斯朝已任內廷警長並數度出任總督，582年率領被史家稱為「不記名冊的 Comes」的野戰軍東行解圍。他把色雷斯與安納托利亞兩地的部隊集結起來，循色雷斯河谷向西南推進，兵臨巴爾幹山關，逼阿瓦爾聯軍放棄對塞薩洛尼基的包圍；同時以陣前會談拖延對手，並派騎兵擾其營地、斷其水源與牧場。解圍之後他回師君士坦丁堡，於582年末與皇帝福卡斯並立為共治者，翌年福卡斯遇弒，莫里斯以「全體羅馬人之愛戴者」之名獨統帝國。史家的筆墨大部分不在戰場而在宮廷：七世紀末的提奧菲拉克特·西莫卡塔（Theophylact Simocatta，約580年代生，約610年卒）留下的《歷史》第三卷是此役最原始也最詳細的記載，但他的重點在外交周旋與敵軍內部的崩解，而非會戰經過；九世紀的提奧法涅斯·君士坦丁堡長老（Theophanes Confessor）則在《編年史》中把582年11月6日寫成巴爾幹山關的一場會戰。塞薩洛尼基方面，編年史記有城中的首長（prytanis）與元老議會拒絕了阿瓦爾人要求交出城內名人的要求，這一節被後世視為城池士氣的例證。阿瓦爾可汗巴顏一系在拜占庭史料中著墨極少，聯軍中的斯拉夫與格皮德首領更是大多無名可考。
peopleEn: The figure around whom every account of this campaign turns is Maurice (Flavius Tiberius Mauricius Emperor, born about 538, killed in 602). He came of a Latin family in Thrace, had already served as magister officiorum and several times as a governor under Phocas, and in 582 led the field army that the historians call a comes in absentia east to lift the siege. He gathered the troops of Thrace and of Anatolia, drove them along the Thracian river valleys towards the south-west, brought them to the Balkan passes, and forced the Avar confederacy to give up its investment of Thessalonica; at the same time he spun the enemy out with parley before the lines and sent cavalry to harry their camp, cut their water and take their grazing grounds. After the relief he returned to Constantinople and was set up in the last months of 582 as co-emperor beside Phocas; when Phocas was murdered in the following year Maurice ruled alone as the beloved of all the Romans. Most of the ink in the sources is not spent on the field but on the court. Theophylact Simocatta (about 580 to about 610), who wrote at the end of the seventh century, left the closest and fullest account of the campaign in the third book of his History, but his emphasis falls on the diplomacy and on the collapse of the enemy from within rather than on the course of any battle. Theophanes Confessor, in the ninth century, records in his Chronographia 6 November 582 as the day of a battle fought at the Balkan passes. On the Thessalonican side the chronicles record that the prytanis of the city and the council of elders refused the demand of the Avars that the leading citizens of the city be handed over, an episode later read as a proof of the garrison's resolve. The Avar kagan of the line of Bayan occupies very little space in the Byzantine sources, and the Slav and Gepid commanders in the confederacy are for the most part nameless.
kits: 卡面上這名希臘重步兵屬於前五世紀的希臘世界：直徑約零點九米的圓盾（hoplon，青銅包邊）、約二點五至二點七米的長矛（dory，鐵或青銅矛頭配白楊木桿）、青銅圓頂頭盔、亞麻胸甲（linothorax）、短劍與備用的短矛，以及護膝護手。到582年，這一兵種作為制式已經不存在：帝國的重步兵穿的是鎖子與環片拼成的罩衣式鎧甲（klibanion），頭戴鐵片盔，手持圓盾與約兩米的長矛（kontos），腰佩直刃劍與曲刀，並攜帶複合弓。希臘重步兵在這場戰役中的位置因此是象徵性的同時也是制度性的：它留下的是「重裝步兵結陣、盾相接、矛齊舉」這一套戰鬥組織方式，也就是在狹窄地形上把對手騎兵的衝鋒壓成可控損失的方法——這恰恰是塞薩洛尼基解圍之戰在隘道中發揮作用的地方。雙方的其他裝備同樣構成對照：阿瓦爾與斯拉夫人以草原反曲複合弓配鋼盔、皮甲與彎刀，靠馬匹自給，作戰方式是高速接近、齊射、脫離；羅馬的守城與攻城器械則有手拉張力弩（cheiroballistra，據普羅科匹烏斯記載六世紀已在役）、配重投石機與固定在城頭的射擊台，圍城一方則用雲梯與撞擊器具，攻城能力有限。
kitsEn: The Greek heavy infantry on the card belongs to the Greek world of the fifth century BC: a round shield of about nine tenths of a metre in diameter (the hoplon, edged with bronze), a spear of some two and a half to two and three quarter metres (the dory, with an iron or bronze head on an aspen shaft), a bronze domed helmet, a linen cuirass (the linothorax), a short sword and a spare javelin, together with greaves and hand guards. By 582 the type no longer existed as a regular arm: the imperial heavy infantry wore a coat of mail and plate assembled as a klibanion, carried iron helmets, a round shield and a spear of about two metres (the kontos), wore at the belt a straight sword and a curved blade, and took a composite bow into the field. The place of the Greek heavy infantry in this campaign is therefore symbolic and at the same time institutional: what it handed down was the organisation of close fighting, the shielded line with spears levelled, and with it the method of converting the charge of enemy cavalry into acceptable losses in narrow ground, which is exactly what told at the passes during the relief of Thessalonica. The rest of the equipment on both sides forms a matching contrast. The Avars and Slavs carried the steppe reflex composite bow with iron helmets, leather armour and sabres, lived off their horses, and fought by closing rapidly, discharging volleys and breaking away. The Roman side on defence and against walls had the cheiroballistra, a hand-drawn tension bow that Procopius shows already in service in the sixth century, counterweight stone throwers and firing platforms fixed to the towers, while the besiegers had ladders and ramming devices and a strictly limited siege capability.
tactics: 這場戰役的戰術骨架只能從地理與制度倒推，具體陣形沒有留下文字，但有幾條線索相當清楚。第一，羅馬不再在開闊地與草原騎兵爭勝，而是把野戰軍用在地形上：莫里斯率軍自色雷斯出發，循河谷與山間通道向西南推進，選擇在巴爾幹山關這一段狹窄通道與敵人接觸，讓對手的騎兵無法展開成衝鋒面。第二，主力是步兵，騎兵擔任兩翼警戒與追擊，弓兵與弩手在陣前及兩側坡地射擊，這正是「盾牆加兩翼投射火力」的結構，也就是卡面那件兵器所代表的方陣思想的直系後裔。第三，進攻次序是先談判再動手：提奧菲拉克特記錄了雙方在陣前的會談，羅馬以拖延換取集結與偵察的時間，同時以騎兵襲擾敵營、截斷水源與牧場，把草原聯軍的戰意與士氣一點一點磨掉。第四，阿瓦爾聯軍內部並非鐵板一塊：斯拉夫人與阿瓦爾人是盟友而非一家，戰利品與駐地的分配長期積怨，當營地遭到盟友攻擊時聯盟當場瓦解，敵軍遂退向多瑙河。第五，戰後羅軍追擊至多瑙河，奪回河東岸的據點與牧場，並在色雷斯的關隘體系上重建防線，築壘設卡、封住通往君士坦丁堡的山道。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of this campaign can only be reconstructed backwards from the ground and the institutions; no text preserves the formations, but several threads stand out clearly. First, Rome no longer sought a decision in the open against steppe cavalry, and instead used the field army on the terrain: Maurice marched out of Thrace along the river valleys and mountain tracks towards the south-west and chose to make contact with the enemy in the narrow defile of the Balkan passes, where the opposing horse could not spread out into a front of charge. Second, the strength was infantry; the cavalry covered the flanks and pursued, while archers and crossbowmen shot from the front of the line and from the slopes on either side, which is the structure of a shielded line with missile fire on the wings, the direct descendant of the phalanx thinking that the weapon on the card represents. Third, the order of operations was to parley before to fight: Theophylact records conversations between the two sides in front of the lines, and Rome used the delay to buy time for concentration and reconnaissance, while cavalry harassed the enemy camp, cut its water and took its grazing grounds, wearing down the will of the steppe confederacy little by little. Fourth, the Avar confederacy was not a single block: the Slavs and the Avars were allies rather than one people, and the distribution of booty and of camp sites had long been a standing grievance, so that when the camp was attacked by its own allies the coalition dissolved on the spot and the enemy withdrew towards the Danube. Fifth, the Romans pursued them to the Danube, recovered the strongholds and pastures on the eastern bank, and rebuilt the line of the Thracian fortified passes, laying strongpoints and barriers across the tracks that led to Constantinople.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且多數帶著爭議。日期：九世紀《編年史》把會戰定在582年11月6日，提奧菲拉克特則把整個行動記在582年之秋到入冬之前；本卡沿用年表的寫法。圍城時長：史家只說「多月」，未給確數，莫里斯的軍隊抵達城下時包圍仍未解除。距離：自色雷斯的集結地到巴爾幹山關約數百公里，行程以日計，史料沒有留下行程表。兵力：兩軍人數都沒有可靠記載，研究一般把六世紀東羅馬野戰軍的規模推估在數千至數萬之間，阿瓦爾聯軍連同斯拉夫與格皮德輔軍同樣只有量級上的猜測，也沒有任何可信的傷亡數字流傳下來。城防：塞薩洛尼基的狄奧多西城牆是這場戰役最硬的數據，現代考古測量給出城牆總周長約四點五至四點八公里，其中海牆約一點三公里、陸牆約三點五公里，牆高約十至十二米，設八座城門與數百座塔樓，牆頂步道足以列弓手。兵器：卡面重步兵的圓盾直徑約零點九米、重約六至八公斤，長矛約二點五至二點七米，頭盔約一點五至二公斤。錢財：史家提到羅馬以贈禮與貢賦換取停戰，但金額完全沒有記錄。
dataEn: There are few numbers that can be checked, and most of them are contested. Date: the ninth-century Chronographia fixes the battle to 6 November 582, while Theophylact places the whole operation in the autumn of 582 and before the onset of winter; this card follows the dating of the battle tables. Duration of the siege: the historians say only that it lasted several months and give no figure, and the blockade was still unbroken when Maurice's army reached the city. Distances: some hundreds of kilometres from the assembly ground in Thrace to the Balkan passes, a march counted in days, with no itinerary preserved. Strength: no reliable figures survive for either army. Studies generally estimate the field army of the sixth-century Eastern Roman Empire at somewhere between several thousand and tens of thousands, and the Avar confederacy with its Slav and Gepid auxiliaries can only be guessed at in the same order of magnitude; no trustworthy casualty figure has come down to us. Fortifications: the Theodosian walls of Thessalonica provide the hardest data in the whole episode. Modern archaeological measurement gives a total circuit of about four and a half to four and three quarter kilometres, of which roughly one and a third kilometre was sea wall and three and a half kilometres land wall, the wall standing some ten to twelve metres high, with eight gates and several hundred towers, and a walkway on the crest wide enough to post archers. Weapons: the round shield of the heavy infantry on the card measures about nine tenths of a metre across and weighs some six to eight kilograms, the spear runs from two and a half to two and three quarter metres, and the helmet about one and a half to two kilograms. Money: the sources record that Rome bought the truce with gifts and tribute, but the amount is not recorded at all.
cause: 打起來有四層理由。對阿瓦爾可汗國來說，六世紀中葉以後草原聯軍在多瑙河上游取得優勢，582年可汗率領聯軍越過多瑙河，先掃掠色雷斯，再直逼塞薩洛尼基，目的是劫掠財富、索取貢賦，並在冬季前取得牧場與駐地；草原政權慣於以圍城作為施壓工具，願意以財物換取退兵，塞薩洛尼基的城牆與商貨正是這樣的目標。對羅馬來說，福卡斯朝十年（571至591年）軍政積弱，多瑙河防線與色雷斯的關隘體系荒廢，邊區的關卡與徵召系統近乎瓦解；新君莫里斯出身色雷斯，正是被進犯的區域，他對邊防虛實有第一手認識，而色雷斯是帝國在歐洲的兵源與糧倉，塞薩洛尼基一旦失守，通往君士坦丁堡的補給線與募兵區就會被切斷。第三層是聯盟的內在張力：斯拉夫人與阿瓦爾人是盟友而非一家，長期受制於可汗，在戰利品與駐地上積怨甚深，這使聯軍在壓力下容易自裂，也讓羅馬不必血戰即可取勝。第四層是帝國自身的戰略轉向：面對質量遠勝自己的草原騎兵，羅馬不能靠會戰取勝，只能靠隘道、城垣、投射火力與外交，把戰爭成本壓到對方無法承受的程度。
causeEn: There are four layers of reason behind the fighting. For the Avar Khaganate, the steppe confederacy had gained the upper hand on the Danube after the middle of the sixth century, and in 582 the kagan led his confederacy across the river, swept Thrace first and then drove straight at Thessalonica, with the object of plundering wealth, pressing for tribute and securing pasture and winter quarters before the cold; steppe polities made a habit of siege as a form of coercion and were willing to withdraw against payment, and the walls and merchandise of Thessalonica were exactly such a target. For Rome, the decade of Phocas from 571 to 591 had left the military administration weak, the Danube line and the system of Thracian passes neglected, and the checkpoints and recruiting system of the frontier close to collapse. The new emperor Maurice came from Thrace itself, from the very region that had been invaded, and knew the state of the frontier at first hand; Thrace was moreover the empire's reservoir of men and grain in Europe, and if Thessalonica fell the supply road and the recruiting ground that fed Constantinople would be cut. The third layer is the internal tension of the coalition: the Slavs and the Avars were allies rather than one people, long held in subjection by the kagan, and deeply aggrieved over the sharing of booty and of camp sites, which made the confederacy liable to split under pressure and allowed Rome to win without a general engagement. The fourth layer is a change of strategy in the empire itself: faced with steppe cavalry of far better quality, Rome could not win by battle, and could only rely on passes, walls, missile fire and diplomacy to press the cost of the war beyond what the enemy could bear.
impact: 直接結果是塞薩洛尼基未陷，帝國在歐洲的門戶得以延續，阿瓦爾聯軍退過多瑙河，邊界線暫時重新固定。但更長期的影響在制度層面：此役之後，莫里斯系統整理歐洲邊防——擴充安納托利亞方面的私兵、重整色雷斯與安納托利亞兩個主題、恢復重建色雷斯的關隘（kleisourai）與長城體系、讓小型機動部隊配合據點去牽制草原騎兵。這套「關隘加主題兵加私兵加外交」的組合，在六世紀末到七世紀初成為帝國對付阿瓦爾與斯拉夫的基本方式，其影子一直延伸到七世紀末。政治上，解圍之功把莫里斯推到權力頂點，他於582年末成為共治皇帝，翌年福卡斯遇弒後獨統帝國；而同一批改革也讓他失去支持，602年他被推翻並遭殺害，東羅馬隨即陷入十餘年的內亂。這場戰役沒有終結草原問題：585年阿瓦爾再犯，586至587年斯拉夫人大規模越境，591年莫里斯渡多瑙河攻擊法蘭克人，598年之後再與阿瓦爾開戰，直到610年赫拉克略即位、626年阿瓦爾被西突厥擊敗，帝國才真正擺脫草原霸權的陰影，而塞薩洛尼基在618年被聯軍攻陷，是這條線上最重的一擊。史學上，此役因提奧菲拉克特《歷史》第三卷而知名，也讓後世看到六世紀末羅馬與阿瓦爾的戰爭是一連串事件而非孤立段落。
impactEn: The immediate result was that Thessalonica did not fall, the empire's gateway in Europe held, the Avar confederacy withdrew across the Danube and the frontier was for the time being fixed again. The longer consequence, however, lay in the institutions. After this campaign Maurice systematically reorganised the European frontier: he expanded the private Bucellarii in Anatolia, reformed the Thracian and Anatolian themes, restored and rebuilt the chain of fortified passes (the kleisourai) and the long wall system of Thrace, and set small mobile columns to work with fixed posts to hold the steppe cavalry in check. This combination of passes, thematic troops, private soldiers and diplomacy became the basic Byzantine answer to the Avars and the Slavs from the late sixth into the seventh century, and its shadow reaches to the end of the seventh. Politically the relief of the city carried Maurice to the summit of power: he became co-emperor in the last months of 582 and ruled alone after the murder of Phocas in the following year. The same circle of reforms, however, robbed him of support, and in 602 he was overthrown and killed, leaving the Eastern Roman Empire in internecine disorder for more than a decade. The campaign did not settle the steppe question. The Avars returned in 585, the Slavs crossed in great numbers in 586 and 587, Maurice himself crossed the Danube against the Franks in 591 and reopened war on the Avars from 598, and only with the accession of Heraclius in 610 and the defeat of the Avars by the Western Turks in 626 did the empire truly slip the shadow of steppe supremacy; the capture of Thessalonica by a combined host in 618 was the heaviest blow on that line. For historians the campaign is known above all through the third book of the History of Theophylact, and it also made clear that the Roman struggles with the Avars in the late sixth century form a chain of events rather than an isolated episode.
result: 結果有兩層。軍事上，塞薩洛尼基解圍成功，阿瓦爾聯軍撤退，羅軍追擊至多瑙河，帝國沒有為此付出可考的大軍損失，史料也沒有留下任何可信的傷亡數字。外交上，史家提到羅馬以贈禮與貢賦換取停戰，這說明當時的帝國並無能力壓倒草原聯軍，只能用錢財買時間，把對手從多瑙河東岸推回去。文字記載上存在落差：提奧菲拉克特著重談判與敵營內部的崩解，把羅軍的推進寫得節制而精確；九世紀《編年史》則把582年11月6日寫成巴爾幹山關的一場會戰，羅軍獲勝。兩者無法互相印證，具體的交戰經過不宜當作定論，但都同意兩點：城市未破，帝國未崩。就卡面這件兵器而言，結論恰恰落在它的傳統上——希臘重步兵作為制式兵種在六世紀早已不復存在，它真正延續下來的是「在狹窄地形上以盾牆限制騎兵展開」這一套戰鬥組織方式，而塞薩洛尼基解圍之戰的關鍵恰恰是隘道；重步兵的價值從來不在單兵格鬥，而在於把對手的衝鋒壓成可以承受的損失。往後看，這場勝利不是終點，而是帝國改變對策的起點：從在多瑙河逐次迎戰，轉向以關隘、主題兵與私兵守住山口，再以外交和贖金換取喘息。
resultEn: The outcome has two layers. Militarily the relief of Thessalonica succeeded, the Avar confederacy withdrew, the Romans pursued them to the Danube, and the empire paid no measurable loss in men, no trustworthy casualty figure having come down to us. Diplomatically the sources record that Rome bought the truce with gifts and tribute, which shows that the empire had no power to crush the steppe confederacy and could only use money to buy time and push the enemy back from the eastern bank of the Danube. The written accounts diverge. Theophylact concentrates on the parley and on the collapse of the enemy camp from within, rendering the Roman advance as measured and exact; the ninth-century Chronographia writes 6 November 582 as a battle fought at the Balkan passes and won by the Romans. The two cannot corroborate one another, and the detailed course of the engagement should not be treated as settled, but both agree on two points: the city was not taken and the empire did not break. As for the weapon on the card, the conclusion falls exactly on its tradition. The Greek heavy infantry as a regular arm had been gone for centuries by the sixth century; what it really handed down was a way of organising close fighting, the shielded line that limited the deployment of cavalry in narrow ground, and the relief of Thessalonica turned on precisely such a defile. The value of heavy infantry has never lain in the individual fighter but in converting the enemy's charge into a loss that can be borne. Looking forward, this victory was not an ending but the beginning of a change of method: from meeting the enemy successively on the Danube to holding the passes with fortified posts, thematic troops and private soldiers, and then buying the time that diplomacy and ransom money could buy.
